title: Partially Filled-In Table

illustrates.quote: Partially Filled-In Tables. Use the same number of columns and/or rows as print when the table shows that only some of the columns and/or rows are filled in. (See Sample 11-18: Partially Filled-in Table on page 11-43.)

print.notes: Three rows are filled with cause/effect sentences; three further rows show only the arrow (→) with both Cause and Effect cells left blank for the reader to complete.
print.printFeatures: Bordered box, ruled lines between rows; the arrow appears in its own narrow middle column in every row, filled or not.

braille.notes: Line 1 placeholder "text". A transcriber's note (line 4) explains the arrow symbol: ".=\\o ,"r >r[@.>" ("[symbol] for arrow"). The arrow column (rendered as ";\\o") appears in every row including the three blank ones (lines 11-13), where the Cause and Effect cells are instead filled with dot-5 guide-dot runs matching rule 11.9.2's instruction to keep the same number of rows/columns as print even where unfilled.
